issues.failure_explanation: The interval has width below 2\eps and contains a with probability at least 1-\alpha, so the point with the stated accuracy is the midpoint (a_l+a_u)/2. The displayed estimator (a_u-a_l)/2 is the half-width; for a narrow interval away from 0 it can differ from a by almost a, so the claimed estimate does not follow.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace (a_u-a_l)/2 by (a_l+a_u)/2 in Proposition prop:m-IQAE and in Algorithm quantum algorithm; the confidence-interval width then gives the stated accuracy.
issues.overall_effect: As written, line 7 of the algorithm need not produce an amplitude within \eps\mathfrak{s}/12 of a, so the final rescaling and the error guarantee in Theorem main theorem lose their justification.
issues.title: Modified IQAE estimator is half the interval width, not the midpoint
issues.why_classification: The repair is a single forced sign change in two places and preserves the error guarantee, confidence level, and all complexity counts.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: the number of qubits used in Algorithm~\ref{quantum algorithm} is at most \mathfrak{C} d^2 (1+\log_2(d\eps^{-1}))
under the additional assumption that $\max_{i=1,\ldots,d}\{\vert x_i \vert \}$ is uniformly bounded in $d \in \N$

issues.failure_explanation: The error estimate is valid for each fixed (t,x), but the displayed qubit, gate, and query bounds contain \mathfrak{c} through \max_i x_i^2. The statement does not assume this maximum is bounded independently of d, so for spot vectors whose coordinates grow with d the bounds need not be polynomial in d; the no-curse conclusion is therefore not established as stated.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add a hypothesis such as \max_{i=1,\ldots,d}\{1,x_i^2\}\le X^2 with X independent of d to Theorem main theorem; the error estimate and the displayed bounds then hold with the same polynomial forms.
issues.overall_effect: The advertised polynomial growth in d and the conclusion of overcoming the curse of dimensionality are unsupported for arbitrary spot vectors; only a uniform-in-d spot bound makes the displayed complexity bounds dimension-polynomial.
issues.title: Main theorem's polynomial-in-d complexity scope lacks a uniform bound on the spot vector
issues.why_classification: This is a limited added hypothesis or scope restriction rather than a new proof architecture, and the comparable bounded-spot-price result survives unchanged.

issues.failure_explanation: Taking the square root of (C_2^2 d^2 2^{n_1+1})^3 gives C_2^3 d^3 2^{(3/2)(n_1+1)}, not C_2 d times the same power of two. With n_1\le 2+\log_2(6\mathfrak{c}d^{5/2}\eps^{-1}), the correct bound is \mathfrak{s}^{-1}\le 2^{13/2}3^2 C_2^3\mathfrak{c}^{3/2}d^{27/4}\eps^{-2}. Consequently the proof yields applications of order d^{27/4}\eps^{-3} and gates of order d^{\max\{7,C_3\}+27/4}, not the displayed d^5 and d^{\max\{12,5+C_3\}}.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Correct the algebra to \mathfrak{s}^{-1}\le 2^{13/2}3^2 C_2^3\mathfrak{c}^{3/2}d^{27/4}\eps^{-2} and adjust the displayed bounds to the resulting exponents. Recovering the stated d^5 and \max\{12,5+C_3\} exponents would require a new error-budget or parameter optimization not present in the source.
issues.overall_effect: The explicit query bound d^5\eps^{-3}\ln(21/\alpha) and the gate exponent \max\{12,5+C_3\} in Theorem main theorem are not proved; the straightforward correction worsens them by d^{7/4}.
issues.title: Proof of main theorem undercounts \mathfrak{s}^{-1} by C_2^2 d^2, invalidating the stated d-exponents
issues.why_classification: The least repair that the source supports materially worsens the explicit complexity exponents; preserving the stated bounds needs a different optimization argument.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Lemma \ref{lemma: quantum addition} (with $n_1 \leftarrow n_1 + m_1$, $n_2 \leftarrow n_2 + m_2$ in the notation of Lemma \ref{lemma: quantum addition})

issues.failure_explanation: For m_1\ne m_2, the cited integer adder adds D_{n_1+m_1,0}(a)=2^{m_1}D_{n_1,m_1}(a) and D_{n_2+m_2,0}(b)=2^{m_2}D_{n_2,m_2}(b), whereas rational addition at a common denominator requires both operands scaled to the same fractional precision. In the final addition of b to an accumulator of precision m=m_1+m_2, the implemented value is accumulator+2^{-m_1}b rather than accumulator+b.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Modify the fractional addition to pad the operand with fewer fractional bits to the common precision max{m_1,m_2} before integer addition, or perform all arithmetic at one declared precision, and update the qubit/gate counts in Lemma quantum affine sum and the dependent loading circuits.
issues.overall_effect: The affine-sum and CPWA loading circuits prove a different function when the grid precision m_1 and coefficient precision m_2 differ; the intercept can be effectively multiplied by 2^{-m_1}. The amplitude analyzed in Theorem main theorem is therefore not the amplitude actually produced by the stated circuit.
issues.title: Fractional addition circuit does not align different binary precisions, so the intercept term is mis-added
issues.why_classification: The fix is a contained construction change rather than a new global architecture, and the intended payoff and polynomial complexity can be preserved, but the circuit as stated computes the wrong affine form.

issues.failure_explanation: Assumption assumption:cov matrix bounds only absolute entries and permits negative correlations. The cited Sidak rectangle lower bound is not justified for negatively correlated centered Gaussians; for perfect negative correlation the upper-orthant intersection can be below the product of marginals. The needed outside-cube estimate is still true by the union bound P(\cup_i\{Y_i>M\})\le\sum_i P(Y_i>M)\le (d/2)M^{-2}, so the defect is repairable without correlation assumptions.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the Sidak/product argument by P(\bm{Y}\notin[0,M]^d)\le\sum_{i=1}^d P(X_i>\ln M)\le (d/2)M^{-2}; no change to the truncation bound or later error budgets is needed.
issues.overall_effect: The truncation-error proof relies on an unjustified correlation inequality, so the downstream error chain is unsupported as written; replacing that step by a union bound restores the same estimate and the whole chain.
issues.title: Sidak lower bound is used although the covariance matrix may have negative correlations
issues.why_classification: The repair is a local replacement of one proof step by a standard union bound and preserves the stated truncation estimate and all downstream guarantees.

issues.failure_explanation: If C_2=2^q, then n_2=1+q and the largest positive dyadic representable in \mathbb{K}_{n_2,m_2} is 2^q-2^{-m_2}<C_2. A coefficient equal to C_2 is allowed by Assumption assumption:CPWA and floors to [C_2]_{m_2}=C_2, which is outside \mathbb{K}_{n_2,m_2,+}; hence the claimed membership and the later encoder E_{n_2,m_2} are not defined for that boundary case.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Take n_2:=2+\lceil\log_2(C_2)\rceil, or explicitly require the rounded coefficients to lie in the representable interval; this changes n_2 by one and leaves the error and complexity conclusions intact.
issues.overall_effect: For power-of-two C_2 with a coefficient equal to C_2, the stated loading of the rounded coefficients is not well-defined, so the circuit construction used in Theorem main theorem is not available for that payoff; the analytical payoff-approximation bounds themselves are not the issue.
issues.title: Encoder range boundary fails when C_2 is a power of two
issues.why_classification: This is a degenerate boundary case fixed by a one-bit increase of the integer register, with no change to the advertised accuracy or polynomial complexity.
